title: Matched regional replacement effects in held-animal wheel decoding
scientific_question: On the same held-animal wheel targets, does replacing a matched non-region population C with region R improve predictive performance given identical background B, and can a frozen participant programme predict competently under both BR and BC?
primary_outputs: Measured signed wheel velocity supplies the participant known answer. The operator also estimates the regional contrast loss(BC)-loss(BR) under outcome-independent matching; its sign is not a preordained answer, and no participant interpretation-accuracy scorer is delivered.

primary.name: Participant BR signed-wheel-velocity mean squared error, reported per region
primary.aggregation: Within each region, equal target timestamps within window, equal windows, all ten matching seeds, equal eligible sessions within animal, then equal animals on the one complete required-operand common support. No outcome-selected region average.
primary.rationale: This is the operative participant-dependent output already computed as candidate_BR_loss. The reference-only regional Holm family is an operator scientific endpoint, not a score of submitted programme or interpretation accuracy.

secondary: Participant BC mean squared error and BR/BC paired reference improvement on exact common support; these accompany the BR primary so degrading BC cannot earn credit.

Operator reference-only scientific estimand loss(BC)-loss(BR), with full six-arm B/R/C/ZERO diagnostics and exact eligibility/failed/unstarted census; this calculation alone is not participant performance.

Per-animal reference replacement effects and source-defined sign test/median intervals/Holm family; candidate competence and regional effects remain descriptive. A participant-submitted numerical-estimand or interpretation response is not currently scored.

comparators.name: Matched BC versus BR
comparators.inputs: BR=B+R and BC=B+C each contain 2k units with identical B; R,C,B disjoint.
comparators.procedure: Use fixed probe/QC/rate strata, rate ratio caliper 1.25 and seeds 0–9 without replacement or outcome-driven relaxation.

comparators.name: Complete six-arm evaluator reference
comparators.inputs: B, BR, BC, R, C and ZERO on original permitted source/query support.
comparators.procedure: Preserve full source-defined six-configuration × five-source-fold selection plus final refits; actual competence remains unmeasured.

comparators.name: Participant competence against corresponding reference arm
comparators.inputs: Exact BR or BC input and common support.
comparators.procedure: Report arm-specific absolute loss and paired reference difference; do not turn a deliberately weak BC into an apparent understanding gain.

nuisance_controls: Match population size, probe, QC category and training-rate stratum, retaining residual rate/quality balance diagnostics.
Preserve one shared complete-ten-seed support object across every compared operand.
Keep whole atlas multiplicity denominator; unavailable p-values retain conservative slots, while prospectively unselected studies are not fabricated tests.
Expose region-specific animal coverage; between-region mean differences with different support are not rankings.
evaluation.uncertainty: Source exact two-sided sign test concerns median directional animal effect, not the mean. Holm correction covers the complete original reference region family; candidate analyses remain descriptive. At 13 nonzero animals the smallest two-sided p is 2^(1-13), so first-step Holm at alpha .05 is impossible for 205 or more regions. Actual R and eligible n_r remain unknown; seeds never enlarge n.
evaluation.failure_policy: Every expected region/session/seed/arm gets a complete, scientific-unavailable, failed or unstarted disposition. Any one unavailable required seed removes the whole session from the common scientific estimator with reasons retained; missing/malformed output, failed fit or uncertain process exit is production failure and cannot become biological exclusion. All planned animals remain in coverage tables.
